page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.metal-96xl is a bare-metal server belonging to the general-purpose compute family, configured to deliver raw CPU density and direct physical hardware access. It is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors providing 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs clocked at 3.9 GHz. System memory totals 1536.0 GB, maintaining an industry-standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Because this is a bare-metal deployment without hypervisor virtualization overhead, full processor and memory allocations are dedicated entirely to guest workloads.

The storage subsystem incorporates 22,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage directly attached to the host, catering to applications with massive I/O throughput demands. Networking performance matches this internal throughput, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 400 Gbps for high-speed inter-service communication and cluster synchronization. The hardware profile does not include dedicated graphics processing units, centering compute entirely on multi-core Intel execution rather than GPU-accelerated workloads.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of high-density local NVMe storage and 400 Gbps networking reduces reliance on external network storage for latency-critical reads and writes. This dense consolidation of compute, memory, and local ephemeral disk optimizes hardware utilization on a single physical footprint. Amazon Web Services m8idb.metal-96xl is appropriately deployed for high-transaction distributed databases, real-time analytics engines, large-scale caching tiers, and enterprise applications requiring massive local data ingestion.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idb.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server built for enterprise workloads requiring extensive local storage and multi-threaded throughput. Driven by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the system provides 192 dedicated physical cores and 384 vCPUs running at 3.9 GHz, paired with 1536 GB of RAM to deliver a balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio. A key capability is its direct-attached storage subsystem, which features 22,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity. Network capabilities are scaled with a baseline bandwidth of 400 Gbps, accommodating high-throughput data replication and low-latency clustering. The hardware configuration lacks dedicated GPU acceleration, focusing entirely on high-density CPU execution and low-latency storage transactions. This hardware profile provides high compute and I/O density on a single bare-metal host, making it particularly effective for large transactional or analytical databases, real-time analytics engines, and high-throughput data ingestion.
